profile.headline: Software Engineer at Microsoft
profile.geoLocationName: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
profile.summary:
I have experience in full-stack web development, Cloud architecture, and Data engineering. I have built five full-stack websites with a PERN stack. I am comfortable with technologies such as Java, C#, JavaScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL, KQL, and Azure. I continually strive to increase my capabilities by improving my knowledge and skill as an engineer.

I am comfortable with Mac, PC, and Linux CLI along with most major software products and IDEs. I also have professional experience with the Adobe Creative Suite.

Fun fact:  I learned to sight-read UEB Braille in three days.

positions.locationName: Washington, District of Columbia, United States

positions.description:

positions.title: Checked - Group Developed
positions.description:
Allows players to challenge each other to chess matches.

HTML | CSS | React | React-Redux | React-router-dom | Postgres | Express | Express-sessions |
Massive | Axios | Chess.js | Chessboard.jsx | Bcrypt | Socket.io | Postman | Jest

Live site: https://www.chessmate.net
Git Repo: https://github.com/ChessMates2018/Checked

Uses Bcrypt to provide a secure and personailzed experience.

Combines props.children, Socket.io and Redux to display the board, determine turn
order, and allow multiple machines to be used.

Endpoint tested with Postman and Unit tested with Jest

positions.title: Writers Corner - Sole Developer
positions.description:
Built to help writers keep track of characters and plot lines.

HTML | CSS | React | React-redux | React-router-dom | Postgres | Express | Express-sessions | Massive | Axios |  Auth-0 | Stripe

Live site: writersincorners.com
Git Repo: https://github.com/FreedomChaser/better-writers-corner

Uses drag and drop in combination with axios and css wrapped in a react component to allow user to have a completely dynamic experience in creating plot lines.

Combines Redux and sessions to ensure that each user has consistent, private access to their storyboards

Creates a radial menu with referent submenus using a combination of CSS and React 

Uses Postgres to not only store plot information but bring it back to the front end in the order dictated by the user.

positions.title: Web Manager/Assistive Technology Coordinator
positions.description:
As Web Manager and Assistive Technology Coordinator I: 
Managed and developed content for the Office of Accessibility Services website using HTML and CSS. 
Lead and trained a staff of between 1 and 8 employees (depending on the semester) in producing alternative text. 
Regularly worked with students in problem-solving using alternative or mainstream technology to meet their needs. 
Researched up and coming technology to try and find better ways to utilize assistive technology.

positions.title: Assistive Technology Specialist
positions.description: As an Assistive Technology Specialist I redesigned documents and textbooks to make them accessible for students with disabilities. My most challenging project was learning, from scratch, how to convert a math book into Nemeth braille--including designing the tactiles in house. I used what I learned in brailling that math book to create an instruction manual on how to braille a math book in order to streamline the process for next time. I also was frequently called upon to do graphic design projects for UVU's Office of Accessibility Services.

positions.title: Writing Tutor
positions.description: As a Writing Tutor I collaborated with students to identify where they were struggling in the writing process and then helped them improve their writing on specific projects, and in general, by teaching them tools to help with identified weak points.

positions.title: Print Specialist
positions.description: As a print specialist I worked with a team of six to handle the printing needs for all of Utah Valley University as well as a few external companies. A few of the things I did include: learning how to format things for print, work with large printers, maintain large printers, and spiral bind books.

positions.title: Co-features Editor
positions.description:
As Co-features Editor I: 
 1. Searched for news or events that would be interesting to our readership.
 2. Found writers to write about these topics or wrote about them myself.
 3. Ensured that the article was print ready and followed AP guidelines.

As part of this job I also occasionally conducted interviews, and frequently fact checked.

positions.title: Writing and Editing Intern
positions.description: At Western Standard Publishing I have gained experience in writing author and title summaries, and formatting books for online publishing using XML.

company.name: The Western Standard Publishing Company, Inc.

volunteerExperiences.role: Mentor Editor in Chief: UVU Journal Intersections
volunteerExperiences.description: As mentor Editor-in-Chief my job is to train Intersections' new Editor-in-Chief in order to make the transition of team leaders a smoother process while maintaining the quality of our journal.

volunteerExperiences.role: Editor In Chief: UVU Journal Intersections
volunteerExperiences.description:
My responsibilities included making sure the Spring 2015 issue of the journal Intersections was well designed, well edited, and printed by the launch party.

As part of this process I lead a team in deciding what pieces should be published, editing these pieces, source checking where needed, typesetting, and print bids.

I was also responsible for the delicate process of smoothing over author's egos when editors stepped on toes, reigning in editors to try and keep them from stepping on toes, and helping build my editors' confidence in their abilities.

With this journal I was given the unique opportunity to take it from acquisitions all the way through printing.

volunteerExperience.role: Editor In Chief: UVU Journal Intersections
volunteerExperience.description:
My responsibilities included making sure the Spring 2015 issue of the journal Intersections was well designed, well edited, and printed by the launch party.

As part of this process I lead a team in deciding what pieces should be published, editing these pieces, source checking where needed, typesetting, and print bids.

I was also responsible for the delicate process of smoothing over author's egos when editors stepped on toes, reigning in editors to try and keep them from stepping on toes, and helping build my editors' confidence in their abilities.

With this journal I was given the unique opportunity to take it from acquisitions all the way through printing.
